beats.narration_text: Everyone will tell you temperature is the creativity dial. Turn it up for wild, turn it down for accurate. That is not what the number does. One line of arithmetic shows what it actually controls — and the answer is not truth.

props.command: Chapter 1 gives me a softmax over the scores 1, 2, 3 and a temperature knob. Show me exactly what temperature changes and what it leaves alone — using the ratio between two outcomes, not a creativity metaphor. Then name the one thing that explanation still cannot establish.

beats.narration_text: Temperature is a concentration control. It decides how concentrated the choice is — not how truthful it is. Get that backwards, and you will trust a number for the wrong reason.

beats.narration_text: Think of the contrast slider on a photo. Slide it up, and bright parts get brighter and dark parts get darker — everything pops. Slide it down, and it all washes toward the same flat grey. But the brightest pixel stays the brightest. Temperature is that slider, run backwards: lower temperature, higher contrast. It changes how much the outcomes differ — never which one is on top. And a high-contrast photo is not a more accurate photo.

beats.narration_text: Here is the whole machine. Three scores — one, two, three. Exponentiate each one, divide by the total, and every outcome gets a probability. At temperature one those come out to zero point zero nine, zero point two four, and zero point six seven. That is the baseline. Every number after this is the same three scores, seen at a different temperature.

sum readout settles at 1.000000 in terracotta — the one accent

beats.narration_text: So ask the machine the only question that isolates temperature: what happens to the ratio between two outcomes?

props.command: Plot p2/p0 for the softmax over scores [1, 2, 3] at T = 0.5, 1, 2. Show the score gap staying fixed at 2 while only T changes, and check each ratio against exp(2/T).
props.runningText: the question the next figure answers

beats.narration_text: Divide outcome two by outcome zero. They share the same total underneath, so it cancels — what is left depends only on the gap between their scores, divided by T. That gap is fixed at two. At temperature zero point five the ratio is fifty-four point six. At one, seven point three nine. At two, just two point seven two — exactly e to the fourth, e squared, and e. No temperature can turn a positive gap negative, so no two outcomes ever swap places.

show.event: title; p₂/p₀ written as two fractions, each over the SAME total Σ exp(z / T) — the definition from B02
on 'so it cancels' the shared total is struck through top and bottom and falls away
what remains resolves into the identity p₂ / p₀ = exp((z₂ − z₀) / T), which rises to the top of the frame
on 'fixed at two' the gap pins: z₂ − z₀ = 2 (fixed), the beat's one terracotta element
table frame lands — T = 0.5 / 1 / 2 and the ordering strip — then each ratio and its bar arrive as the voice says it
on 'exactly e to the fourth, e squared, and e' the e-column lands: = e⁴, e², e¹
on 'no two outcomes ever swap places' the ordering strip darkens and grows — the conclusion the cancellation made inevitable

beats.narration_text: Now the limit — what this does not establish. Push the temperature down and the best outcome dominates, but it never becomes certain: at zero point one the worst still holds two times ten to the minus nine. Temperature zero is refused outright — the function raises a value error. Concentration is not correctness. Turn the contrast all the way up on a photo of the wrong person, and all you get is a sharper picture of the wrong person.

show.event: a single temperature axis sweeps down from T = 1 toward 0
the outcome-2 bar grows toward full height but a visible sliver always remains for outcome 0
callout at T = 0.1: p₀ = 2.061060e-09 — 'small, not zero'
T = 0 is reached; the axis stops dead and a refusal card snaps in terracotta: ValueError: Need logits and a positive finite temperature
the bars dim and one line replaces them: 'concentration ≠ correctness'
that line holds alone on the white canvas
the three swatches from B01A return above the refusal card, at full high contrast — the analogy called back on the boundary beat
the line 'a sharper picture of the wrong person' lands beneath 'concentration ≠ correctness'

beats.narration_text: So, one page. Temperature divides the score gap before exponentiating, so it rescales every ratio at once. The ordering is untouched — outcome two wins at every temperature we tested. The sampled counts agree: eight hundred forty-nine, six hundred thirty, four hundred sixty-nine, at seed seven. And none of that is evidence the answer is right.

show.event: Claude artifact page opens on the cream ground, titled 'Temperature — one page'
line 1 reveals: the mechanism
line 2 reveals: ordering untouched
line 3 reveals: the seed-7 counts
line 4 reveals in terracotta: the boundary

artifactLines: Mechanism: p_i/p_k = exp((z_i − z_k)/T). Normalization cancels, so T rescales every ratio at once.
Ordering [2, 1, 0] never changes. Seed 7, n = 1000: outcome 2 is drawn 849 / 630 / 469 times at T = 0.5 / 1 / 2 — at T = 2 the full count is 202 / 329 / 469, still in order.
Limit case: at T = 0.1 the worst outcome still holds 2.061060e-09 — small, not zero. T = 0 raises ValueError.
Boundary: concentration is not correctness. T cannot add information the program never received.
Reproduced: main.py run 3x under Python 3.9.10 and 3.12.9 — identical counts each time. Matched on these versions, not proven universal.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here is the prompt: take a softmax over the scores one, two, three. Compute p two over p zero at T equals zero point five, one, and two, and check each value against e to the two over T. Now change only the middle score, to two point five, and recompute: tell me which ratios moved, which stayed fixed, and why the fixed one had to stay fixed. Run it, and watch which one holds still — that is the identity doing the work.
